Comparison: 1-18-2018 and before.
CLINICAL DATA: 41 year old man with small bowel obstruction,
possible rectal abscess, rule out pneumothorax.
Findings: AP portable view of the chest taken on 1/18/2018 at 10:54 hours
demonstrates interval removal of the left subclavian venous
catheter. The projection is right rotated, however, there is
interval development of a small to moderate left pneumothorax.
There is new vascular crowding at the left lower lung region
suggesting pneumothorax related atelectasis. The right lung is
clear. Residual contrast is again seen in the right upper quadrant
of the abdomen. There is a G-tube in place.
AP portable view of the chest taken on 1/18/18 demonstrated
interval increase of the left pneumothorax and also increasing left
lower lobe atelectasis. There is suggestion of a mediastinal shift
to the right with increased distances between the left ribs. These
are worrisome for a tension pneumothorax.
AP portable view of the chest taken on 1/18/2018 at 17:52 hours
demonstrated interval placement of a left sided chest tube with the
tip that passed midline. There is re-expansion of the left lung
with a tiny residual left pneumothorax. There is interval
development of trace amount of right base atelectasis. There is a
plate-like atelectasis in the left mid lung.
Impression: 1. INTERVAL DEVELOPMENT OF A MODERATE LEFT SIDED PNEUMOTHORAX WITH
SUGGESTION OF TENSION.
2. PLACEMENT OF A LEFT SIDED CHEST TUBE THAT PASSED MIDLINE,
POSSIBLY INTO THE RIGHT HEMITHORAX.
3. TINY LEFT PNEUMOTHORAX REMAINS.
Summary: 4: Possible Significant Abnormality/Change, may need
action.
